claims.finding: The two large convenience-fuel peers whose reporting windows bracket Casey's May-July quarter both printed roughly a 9-cent-per-gallon year-on-year fuel-margin expansion with inside-store sales holding: Couche-Tard's quarter to 26 April 2026 showed US road-transportation fuel margin of 52.44 cpg, up 9.17 cpg, with US same-store merchandise revenue +3.4% and US same-store fuel volume only -2.1%; Murphy USA's June quarter (reported 2026-08-05) showed total fuel contribution of 40.6 cpg against 32.0 cpg a year earlier, total gallons +3.9%, same-store gallons +0.5%, and CEO Mindy West said the second half 'could be even stronger'.
claims.corpus_ref: docs/3e335dae4f51e41b6447b25b5c94730fe2242d96.txt (snapshots/20260907T152430Z.json item 22) and docs/7d7c214e533df697571cb48e92abe53e1d5ff9c7.txt (snapshots/20260908T152241Z.json item 15, Couche-Tard FQ4 FY2026 release dated 2026-06-22)
claims.why_not_priced: Casey's fuel margin is the metric that produced the last print's +20.3% reaction (46.9 cpg, a company record, and EPS of $4.37 against a $3.31 consensus), and the consensus line items captured here forecast only revenue of $5.65bn on 936.9m gallons with grocery same-store +3.6% and prepared-food same-store +4.3% - i.e. the sell side is modelling normal inside-store growth and gives no visible credit for a repeat of record cents-per-gallon. If the peer read were priced, CASY would not have fallen from $854.21 on 08/24 to $740.49 by the 09-08 midday mark, -14.2% over 20 sessions and 20% off its 52-week high, while its own estimate revisions were moving higher. The peer numbers themselves are public but they sit in a Couche-Tard release from 22 June and a regional Arkansas business paper from 5 August, and nothing in this 42-document capture connects them to Casey's July-quarter fuel line.
claims.independence: A third, independent source points the same way on the price environment that drives the margin: https://energyfactbook.com/why-are-gas-prices-high/ (docs/ce2f8f1204ac4c27fa305e89296c10ac2e9a5f00.txt) documents WTI running from $60/bbl in January 2026 to $102 in May and back to $91.48 on 1 September, retail regular at $4.07/gal on 31 August against $3.15 a year earlier (+29.4%), with EIA attributing it to reduced Strait of Hormuz shipments - a falling-wholesale, high-volatility path across exactly the May-July window, which is the condition Casey's management has itself credited for margin outperformance. A fourth source, https://www.optionstradingreport.com/2026/09/caseys-faces-a-record-price-fuel-quarter/, independently notes diesel hit a record $5.85/gal in the quarter, past the June 2022 mark.

claims.finding: Short interest as of 14 August was 1,143,057 shares, down 32.3% from 1,688,551 on 30 July, leaving only 3.1% of shares short and a 4.0-day short-interest ratio - so the 14% drawdown from 08/24 to the print was long liquidation into an already-covered short base, not short pressure.
claims.why_not_priced: Short-interest prints lag two weeks and are rarely folded into a pre-earnings view; the observation here is not that shorts are a catalyst but that they are absent, which removes the mechanical squeeze component from any upside reaction and is a reason my first finding is worth half the median move rather than all of it. It is signed negative because it caps the tail I would otherwise assign.
claims.independence: Corroborated by volume in quote.json: the 08/27 and 08/28 sessions traded 454,500 and 442,100 shares against a 350,780 20-day average - elevated but only 1.3x, which is a distribution pattern rather than a forced-cover or panic pattern. This finding is independent of the fuel-margin finding in source but deliberately cuts against its magnitude, not its sign.
